newsitem.title: GREECE: Thousands march to remember Athens student revolt.
newsitem.headline: Thousands march to remember Athens student revolt.

text.p: About 5,000 demonstrators marched through Athens on Sunday to commemorate a bloody student uprising 23 years ago against the military junta that ruled Greece from 1967 to 1974.
Police on hand to prevent possible violence outnumbered the demonstrators by around three to one.

The marchers, chanting "The Polytechnic lives" and the popular anti-dictatorship slogan "Bread, Education, Freedom", reached the United States embassy, the focal point of the demonstration, without incident.

The annual march commemorates the day in 1973 when the U.S.-backed junta sent in tanks to crush the student revolt at the Athens Polytechnic. At least 20 students died but many historians put the number much higher.
The ruthless action ended whatever limited sympathy the junta still had with the public and it fell the following year.
The memorial march was headed by Polytechnic students carrying the bloodied Greek flag of the 1973 revolt and black-clad mothers of killed students carrying a banner reading "The Polytechnic Lives."
Police said they deployed the unusually heavy number of men around the capital to head off any attemps by rioting youths to take over the Athens Polytechnic.
After last year's march, hundreds of youths describing themselves as anarchists occupied the school, setting fire to it and causing considerable property damage.

The November 17 march is usually peaceful but self-styled young anarchists often rampage through central Athens after it is over. In 1995, 470 youths were arrested after two days of clashes and more than 100 of them were given jail terms for taking part in the riots.
